source: BMW N52B30 3.0 L I6 as used by the game's car_sedan (data/engines/n52b30_3l_na.json). displacement_l 2.996 [C: the engine file's own cited 2,996 cc (85 mm bore x 88 mm stroke x 6 = pi/4 * 8.5^2 * 8.8 * 6 = 2994 cm3), the only cited number in this file]. Every other number is [AS]/[D] and says so. Engine lump: 27060 J/K per litre [AS] = 18 kg/L participating metal [AS: the N52 has an aluminium-magnesium crankcase and an aluminium head, so less iron than the class's 25 kg/L at 62 % cast iron; 18 kg/L = 54 kg of block and head for 3.0 L, assumed from the 165 kg engine mass in the engine file, no citation fetched] x 900 J/(kg K) [C: aluminium, the class file's own value; the thin iron liners and Mg shell ignored] = 16200 + 3.0 L/L coolant [AS, class] x 1065 kg/m3 x 3400 J/(kg K) = 10863 [class]. Within 2 % of the class 26600, i.e. the Al-Mg block does not change the thermal mass materially. Oil lump 7600 J/K per litre [AS: class value, 2.25 L/L oil is 6.7 L for 3.0 L, a plausible N52 sump]. oil.hydrodynamic_fraction 0.2 [D]: this engine's motoring_torque_nm_vs_rpm is i4_2l_na.json's curve scaled by the displacement ratio 1.5 (see the engine file), so it carries the same Heywood FMEP split as engine_thermal/i4_2l_na.json, whose 0.2 overrides the class 0.5 for exactly this correlation (hydrodynamic share 0.30 bar of 1.47 bar at 2000 rpm); cold-start behaviour at -30 C was not re-checked for the 3.0 L (the game starts warm). wall_heat_fraction 0.20, friction_to_oil_fraction 0.30, motoring_friction_fraction 0.6, the conductances, pump (10 L/min per krpm per L, 180 L/min at 6000 rpm) and the 88 -> 100 C thermostat are the class defaults [AS] unchanged (class_si_passenger.json carries their derivations).
